newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says no worry on foreign speculation on T$.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says no worry on foreign speculation on T$.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Saturday the island had enough financial power to defend its currency from foreign speculation.
"Our situation is totally different from Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia," Sheu told a seminar.
"Our situation is stable like a mountain. We won't have any problem, please don't worry."
Sheu said foreign speculators had tried to manipulate Taiwan's foreign exchange market.
"Foreign speculators intend to manipulate our market, but they also are a little bit scared, because we have enough bullets to defend the Taiwan dollar in a reasonable level," Sheu said.
Southeast Asian nations' currencies have plunged in recent weeks due to heavy foreign speculation, but the Taiwan dollar has been comparatively stable.
The central bank has let the Taiwan dollar fall some four percent against the U.S. dollar since late July to reflect part of the greenback's strength overseas.

Taiwan's huge foreign exchange reserves have given the central bank strong back-up to defend its currency. At the end of June, Taiwan's foreign reserves reached US$90.03 billion, the world's third biggest after Japan and China.
Sheu vowed that Taiwan would continue to open its financial markets and make the island an Asia-Pacific financial centre.
